title: Claim Payments and the FloodGuard Cancellation Credit
content:
**Claims manual note — FloodGuard Private Flood Policy**

Claim payments issued on the policy within the 12 months before the cancellation is processed reduce the credit: a building or contents payment makes the premium fully earned, so no credit and no fee return are due; loss-avoidance reimbursements alone are deducted from the credit in the amount paid; and with no such payment nothing is deducted.

**Payments read.** The flood claim payments on this policy's claim files issued in the 12 months before the day the cancellation is processed, sorted by coverage part: building and contents payments on one side; loss-avoidance reimbursements — the reimbursement of sandbags, fill and pumping to protect the building from imminent flood — on the other.

| Building or contents payment in the 12 months | Loss-avoidance reimbursement in the 12 months | Effect on the cancellation credit |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes or no | The premium is fully earned: nothing is credited and no part of the policy fee is returned |
| No | Yes | The credit is reduced by the total loss-avoidance amount paid in the 12 months |
| No | No | Nothing is deducted |

**Questions answered (hypothetical inputs)**

*A building payment was issued 13 months before the cancellation is processed and nothing has been paid since.* The payment lies outside the 12 months and is not read; with no other payment in the window, nothing is deducted.

*The only payment in the 12 months is a loss-avoidance reimbursement of 400.00, and the credit stands at 650.00 before this deduction.* The credit is reduced by 400.00, to 250.00.

*A contents payment of 2,500.00 and a loss-avoidance reimbursement of 300.00 were both issued in the 12 months.* The contents payment makes the premium fully earned; no premium is credited and no part of the policy fee is returned.
